verdict: A competent dark-glass concept with a clear Idea, Team, Agent, Mark logic. The opening frame, the dark inhale at 8.3 s and the final lockup are good, and they fix most of v1's flat, inverted look. It still falls short of premium-agency level for four reasons. The climax is a short pastel brightness wash, not a designed peak. The payoff word АГЕНТ is on screen too briefly to read. Fast cubes show cheap-looking stepped motion blur. The lockup is clean but flat and slightly misaligned, and the background is lighter and more banded than the dark brand. Fixing the hit, the АГЕНТ timing and the blur would move it toward 7.5-8.
strengths: Frame 0 (still_00.00) is a strong, memorable opening. One large glowing cyan cube floats in a field of near-black glass cubes with thin blue rim lights. Scale variation, defocused foreground cubes and dust give real value contrast and depth. It reads dark and on-brand, unlike v1.

ИДЕЯ at 2.2 s and КОМАНДА at 4.0 s are legible. Ice-white and blue cubes with bloom sit on dark blue with good luminance contrast, and the Cyrillic glyphs are unambiguous. From the 0.5 s overview, ИДЕЯ holds about 0.8-1.0 s and КОМАНДА about 1.2 s. That is enough to read them.

The inhale at 8.30 s (still_08.30) sets up the hit well. The wall is crisp and dark, with cell-edge rim lights and the carved figure readable as negative space. The step up to the 8.40 flash is a real contrast move. The scale punch (about 440 px to about 550 px wide at 1280) gives physical impact.

The final lockup (still_12.50 and still_14.50) is clean and holdable. It has a bold Manrope-style title with 'AI' in brand cyan, a flat vector mark, a thin accent rule and a tracked mono tagline, so the hierarchy is clear. The name is spelled 'HackAlem AI' as required. It will work as the start of a longer presentation.

The swirl into the mark (7.0-7.8 s) pays off the whole build. The wall reads as the brand mark, with blue corner cells and rim highlights. The title reveal (10.5-11.5 s) is a restrained blur-and-fade, letter by letter.

flaws.flaw: The climax is a washed-out pastel flash, not a white-hot peak. It lasts about 0.2 s (peak 8.43-8.60) and then deflates. At 8.50 the whole frame lifts to mid-blue. Mean luminance rises from 38 to 114, the halo below the wall reaches about (104,157,187), the left edge goes from (0,12,38) to (0,49,102), and the wall turns frosted ice-blue. The brand's near-black is lost, and the carved figure becomes hard to read as light on light. The wall stays intact, with no visible shockwave ring, ejected debris or shake. After 8.70 the wall shrinks from about 556 px back to about 444 px wide by 9.2 s. It is dimmer and smaller than the pre-hit inhale. From 8.83 to 9.5 the carved-figure area shows muddy grey translucent cubes, which is off-brand. The vertical light streaks at the left and right of the figure (rows 4-6, present 8.30-9.2) look like smeared emissive sprites, not light bursting through. The beauty shot is effectively missing.
flaws.why_it_matters: This is the one frame the brief says must be a real visual peak, and the customer's complaint about v1 was a weak climax. A milky flat flash at 38 to 114 mean luminance reads as an exposure change, not an event. A drop in scale and brightness right after the peak kills the payoff, and the grey interior looks dirty on a premium render.
flaws.fix: Rebuild the hit as a short, sharp, additive event. (1) Frames 8.400-8.533: drive the wall core to near-clipped white (#FFFFFF, bloom threshold lowered) while keeping the surrounding background near its pre-hit value (max about (0,40,90)). Apply the flash as additive light on and around the wall, not a global lift or a full-frame halo. (2) Add an expanding thin cyan shockwave ring from the wall centre, 8.40 to 8.95 s, radius 0 to about 0.9x frame height, fading out. Add 20-30 edge cubes ejected radially with velocity-aligned motion blur. (3) Camera punch-in 1.00 to 1.12 over 3 frames, ease back over about 0.5 s, plus decaying 4-6 px shake over 0.25 s. (4) Hold the wall at full scale and fully lit until about 9.6 s. Do not shrink it until the glide begins. Add a slow 4-6 degree yaw so the glass catches rim light. (5) Set the back-plate cubes inside the carved figure to emissive cyan to white, or to deep navy, never grey. Replace the vertical streak sprites with a soft radial light leak through the figure.
flaws.evidence: hit_sequence_8.3-9.2s.png; still_08.30, still_08.50, still_09.20; pixel sampling of still_08.30 and still_08.50 (mean luminance 38.3 to 113.8; halo (104,157,187)); wall width measured from the hit-sequence cells (about 220 px to 276 px at half scale, back to about 222 px).

flaws.flaw: The third word, АГЕНТ, is readable for only about 0.5-0.7 s. At 5.5 s (still_05.50) only the first two letters are crisp and the rest is a drifting cloud. It is complete at about 6.0 s and is already breaking up by 6.5 s (overview 5.5, 6.0, 6.5). By comparison ИДЕЯ holds about 0.9 s and КОМАНДА about 1.2 s. In the 360 px phone sheet the АГЕНТ tile shows only a scatter of cubes with no word. АГЕНТ is also lit inconsistently with its neighbours. ИДЕЯ is ice-white, КОМАНДА is the darkest and most saturated mid-blue, and АГЕНТ is white-cyan only briefly.
flaws.why_it_matters: АГЕНТ is the payoff of 'Идея, Команда, Агент' and the product idea. A five-letter word needs about 1 s or more to be read. The film's 'words stay long enough to read' requirement is not met on the key word, and the sequence feels rushed exactly where it should land.
flaws.fix: Re-time the sequence. Have the АГЕНТ cubes land in reading order (left to right, about 40 ms stagger) so the word is legible by 5.4 s. Hold the formed word from 5.5 to 6.5 s (at least 1.0 s). Start the swirl-to-mark at about 6.6 s instead of 6.4 s, and take the time from the 7.8-8.4 s inhale or trim the КОМАНДА hold by about 0.2 s. Normalise brightness across the three words (same bloom and cube albedo, with the third word the brightest). Give КОМАНДА more bloom and a lighter cube tint so it does not sink into the navy.
flaws.evidence: still_05.50.png; overview_0-7s.png (frames 4.5-6.5); phone_size_360px.png (tile 4); still_04.00 for relative brightness.

flaws.flaw: Motion blur on fast cubes shows stepped ghost copies, not a smooth smear. Cubes show 'venetian-blind' stacks of semi-transparent slices, for example the right-hand group at 1.20 s (x 1140-1200, y 380-500), at 3.00 s (about 560-600, 130-190 and about 445-495, 570-650) and the cube at about (1000, 300) at 7.40 s. This points to a low sample count in the sub-frame blur. In the formed words the cubes read as flat, milky, uniformly lit ice tiles with soft rounded edges. There is little visible refraction or internal depth, so they look closer to LED-matrix pixels than glass. The words are viewed frontally, with a flat orthographic look and no perspective drift. All three words use the same scatter, fly-in and hold choreography.
flaws.why_it_matters: Stepped blur and flat, milky cubes are the clearest tells of a cheap render and are visible at full size. The customer's complaints about v1 included choppy motion and flat, depthless rendering. The formed words are the parts held on screen longest, and they have the least depth.
flaws.fix: Raise the motion-blur sample count to 16-32 jittered sub-frames per frame at a 180 degree shutter, or replace it with velocity-vector stretch plus an additive fading trail. Cap landing speeds so cubes do not cross more than about 40 px per sub-frame. For the formed words, add a slow camera dolly or yaw of 3-6 degrees with parallax across the wall. Give each cube a darker core, a Fresnel rim and a slight emissive gradient (brighter edges, darker centre) so it reads as glass and not as frosted plastic. Add some cube-to-cube emissive variation. Vary the choreography per word, for example a different entry vector for each.
flaws.evidence: still_01.20, still_03.00, still_05.50, still_07.40; crop of still_01.20 (right side); still_02.20 and still_00.00 for cube material.

flaws.flaw: The wall-to-logo transition and the lockup lose the 3D language, and the lockup is slightly unbalanced. At 10.50 s the wall is a flat solid-blue square at left (about x 270-610) with the right 55 % of the frame empty. By 11.0 s the mark has moved further left (about x 100-380) and shrunk, so there are two separate moves, not one continuous glide. The final mark is a flat sticker with faint seam lines and measured fill about (0,138,219) = #008ADB, roughly 10 % darker than brand #009AF0. It has no rim light or glow, so it feels like a template title card after a lit 3D scene. The text block is top-biased. The title cap-top aligns near the mark top (about y 230 against 225), but the tagline ends at about y 425 against the mark bottom at about y 495. The block centre is about y 328 against the mark centre at y 360, which is about 48 px at 1080p. The rule (about 373 px) matches neither the title (about 735 px with 'AI') nor the tagline (about 680 px), so there are three different right edges (about x 1165, 1112 and 803). The mono tagline is also small against the title, with a cap height about 1/4.7 of the title's.
flaws.why_it_matters: The lockup is the frame that holds and starts the presentation. It is on screen for the last 3-5 s. Small alignment errors and a flat, off-colour mark read as unfinished to an art director, and the drop in production value from the 3D scene to the end card undercuts the premium feel.
flaws.fix: Make the glide a single move. Use one ease-in-out from the wall's position at 9.2 s to the final lockup position and scale, over about 9.5-10.8 s. Do not stop at x about 440 first, and do not leave a dead right half at 10.5 s (start the title rise at about 10.3 s). Rebuild the lockup grid. Set the mark fill to exactly #009AF0. Add a subtle edge bevel or inner rim and a soft glow at about 15-20 % so it keeps the glass language, and fade the seam grid to under 3 % or remove it. Align the text block to the mark: title cap-top on the mark top edge (or row 2), tagline baseline on the mark bottom edge, with gap set accordingly (enlarge the title about 10-15 % if needed). Set the rule width equal to 'HackAlem' (about 590 px) or to the tagline width, and share one right edge. Raise the tagline size by about 15-20 %.
flaws.evidence: still_10.50, still_11.00, still_12.50, still_14.50; overview_7.5-14.5s.png; pixel sample of mark fill (0,138,219) at (150,300) of still_12.50; crop of the lockup (measured edges at 1280 scale).

flaws.flaw: The background is lighter and bluer than the brand's dark base and shows gradient banding. The scene mid-field is about (0,49,103) = #003167 (top centre of the holds). Brand base is #060B16, which only appears at the corners (about (0,5,24)). The result is a saturated royal-blue radial glow, not a near-black base with a blue volumetric beam from above, as on the site hero. The holds contain visible concentric rings in the glow, with 331 distinct 1-LSB steps across one row at y=100 in still_14.50. The rings are clearly visible in the 4x contrast-boosted check and faintly visible unboosted around the title.
flaws.why_it_matters: The customer explicitly wanted the dark brand, not a blue wash. A static hold of 3-5 s shows banding on any projector or conference screen, and flat dark gradients are where compression artifacts show most. The missing beam drops the one brand lighting cue the site has.
flaws.fix: Lower the ambient glow to peak at about (6,28,60) and keep the outer 40 % of the frame at #060B16. Add a narrow, soft volumetric beam from the top centre (cone about 12-15 degrees, 8-12 % opacity, slight noise in it), as on the site hero. Add 1-2 LSB monochrome dither or fine film grain (about 1.2-1.5 % luminance noise) before encode on the whole frame. Encode with a lower CRF (about 14-16 for H.264, or 10-bit) and check the 12-15 s hold for banding.
flaws.evidence: pixel sampling of all stills (e.g. still_12.50 at (640,100) = (0,49,103), corners (0,5,24)); row-step count on still_14.50; 4x-enhanced crop of still_14.50.

flaws.flaw: The corner elements are tiny, redundant and not protected from the scene. The top-left 'hackalem.ai' (lowercase, with .ai) differs from the lockup's 'HackAlem AI', so the name appears in two forms. The top-right tagline 'AGENTIC-AI ХАКАТОН · АСТАНА' is about 14 px high at 1280 in pale mid-blue and is repeated in full in the lockup. Cubes and bloom pass over it. At 1.20 s a glowing cube sits on the tagline and washes it out, and at 0.50 s a dark cube overlaps the 'a' of the logo. In the 360 px phone sheet both corner elements are illegible.
flaws.why_it_matters: A name shown two ways in one 15 s film weakens recognisability. A tagline that cannot be read and is then shown again at the end adds clutter during the build without adding information. Collisions with cubes make the frame look unmanaged.
flaws.fix: Keep only the corner logo (mark plus wordmark) at about 70 % opacity. Remove the corner tagline and leave it for the lockup. Keep the corner HUD above the cube layer and give it a small dark gradient scrim so bloom cannot wash it out. Alternatively fade both corners out during the hit build (from about 7.8 s) so the name first appears in full at the lockup. If a lowercase corner logo is the official site mark, keep it, but make 'HackAlem AI' the only form of the name in the lockup text.
flaws.evidence: still_00.00, still_00.50, still_01.20; phone_size_360px.png; crop of the corner logo from still_00.00.

unverifiable: Real-time motion quality: smoothness, easing and whether the cube flights feel choppy. I only had stills sampled every 0.5 s plus one 0.033 s-step sheet of the hit, so I cannot judge motion curves, judder or frame pacing.
The exact readable time of each word. Overview frames are 0.5 s apart, so the AGENT window (about 5.8-6.3 s) is estimated from the 5.5, 6.0 and 6.5 s frames and could be off by about +/-0.25 s.

The sheen across the mark during the 12.1-15 s hold. The 12.5 s and 14.5 s stills differ by a mean of only about 0.9 (on a 0-765 sum scale) in the mark region, so no sheen is visible in those two frames. It may occur in between.

Whether the global brightness jump at the hit (mean luminance about 38 to about 114 within roughly 0.1 s) has any flash or photosensitivity concern when played. I cannot assess the rate of change from stills.
How the corner logo and tagline fade out near 9.7 s, because I have no frame between 9.5 and 10.0 s that isolates it. They are present at 9.2 s and absent at 10.5 s.

Whether the first letter of 'АГЕНТ' is Cyrillic or Latin (the brief spells it 'AГЕНТ'). Both look identical in the pixel font. I also cannot check fidelity of the mark and the carved figure to the original brand vector.

Anything about sound: sync of the hit to the 8.40 s flash, loudness, tone or mix. I read only the event list, which puts the main hit events at 8.40 s with the 'crunch' at 8.13 s and matches the visual flash timing. The brief says nobody has listened to it, and I did not evaluate it.
Compression versus source quality. I cannot tell whether the stepped motion blur and banding come from the render or from the encode of the review files.

verdict: Everything here is inferred from measurements, the event list and the spectrogram. I have not heard the film. On paper the mix is technically clean. The build resolves into the hit in the right key (A major, then D major), and the hit is frame-accurate to the picture flash. The sound arc is weaker than the picture arc. The build is a flat, repeated loop of 16th-note arps and ascending runs, and the ML listeners label it as video-game or mallet music. The 'inhale' before the hit barely dips. The brand lockup (title, rule, tagline, hold) is the quietest, thinnest and least-accented part of the film, and the ML scorers rate that tail weakest. The hit stacks about ten layers on one frame, and a lot of its weight is probably sub-bass that phones and laptops will not reproduce. This is a competent 6 out of 10, not a premium-agency 8 or above.
strengths: Technical hygiene is good: -14.66 LUFS integrated, -2.14 dBTP, 0 clipped samples, PLR 12.5 dB, LRA 4.7 LU, DC 0.00001, 14 of 16 checklist items OK (audio_eval_full.txt sections 1, 4, 6). That leaves headroom for AAC.

Spectral balance is inside the p10-p90 band of the 43 real tracks at every octave, with a slope of -1.7 dB/oct. 31.5 Hz is -2.1 dB and 63 Hz is -3.8 dB against the median, and the share below 150 Hz is 23.9% (p44). Inference: the v1 complaint of bass-heavy, thin, toy-like sound is not repeated in the averages. The mix does not read as boomy or harsh overall (2-8 kHz share 6.7%).

Small-speaker translation looks fine globally. Loudness falls only -0.7 LU with a 150 Hz high-pass (laptop) and -1.5 LU with a 300 Hz high-pass (phone), around p63-p74 of real music. Bass below 150 Hz has L/R correlation 0.97, so it is mono-safe.

There is a clear build-to-hit loudness step. Momentary loudness is about -16 LUFS at 8.0 s and -10 at 8.5 s (max -10.4), roughly +6 LU. It then decays gently to -16 by 12 s. No window has negative L/R correlation.

Hit sync is frame-accurate. hit_sequence_8.3-9.2s.png shows 8.367 s still dark and the flash starting on the 8.400 s frame, which matches the 8.400 s audio events. The 8.4 s downbeat sits on the kick grid (1.6 s + n x 0.4 s, 150 BPM).

The harmony is coherent with the picture. The land notes and the stab chords stay in D minor / Dorian (C4 D4 E4 F4 A4 C5, then Bbmaj7/D, then Gm9). From 7.0 s to 7.9 s the arps and land:mark notes (C#5 E5 A5 C#6 E6 A6) form an A major / A7 dominant. The hit then lands on D major (bells D5 A5 D6 F#6), the sparks descend in D major pentatonic, and the sting is a D major triad. The V to I turn under the D minor to D major brief is deliberate and sound.

The ML listeners report no noise, distortion or static (AST noise/static/distortion at or near 0.00; Audiobox PQ 7.79 overall, minimum window 6.98, above the real-track maximum window of 6.58; CLAP margin +0.31). These tools are trained on music and have limited validity for a 15 s sting, so this supports 'not dirty' rather than 'premium'.

flaws.flaw: The build is a flat loop with the same gesture four times. A continuous 16th-note arp (0.1 s spacing, -22 to -32 dB) runs under a 4-on-the-floor kick from 1.6 s to 7.6 s. All four word-landings use the same device: a rising 7-8 note run plus tock/click per cube, then a chord stab. The runs top out at the same level every time: idea -16.3 dB, team -16.0, agent -16.2, mark -16.0. Momentary loudness is 3 LU of sawtooth between -15 and -18 for 8 s, and it starts at its second-loudest value (-13 at 0 s) before falling to -18 at 2.5 s. The only escalation is kick (-16.5, then -14.5, then -12.5 dB) and bass, which are sub-heavy and drop out on a phone. The ML listeners read the build as 'Glockenspiel 0.21 / Mallet percussion 0.18' (0-3 s) and 'Video game music 0.48' (6-9 s). CLAP's best prompt in the 6-9 s window is '8-bit chiptune video game music' (0.407). Whole-film CLAP gives chiptune 0.39 against 'clean premium tech logo sting' 0.45.
flaws.why_it_matters: 'Toy-like' was a named v1 complaint, and the sound has to carry the sense of development. A repeating mallet and arp loop with no timbral or level progression reads as a game or ringtone bed. It also means the hit is the only dynamic event in the first 8 s.
flaws.fix: 1) Thin the arp: gate it to 8ths from 0.4 s to 4.8 s and use 16ths only from 6.4 s to 7.8 s, and cut its level 3-4 dB with a low-pass. 2) Automate a low-pass sweep on pad, arp and bed from about 1.2 kHz at 0 s to about 9 kHz at 8.3 s, so the build opens up. 3) Escalate the land-run peaks so the momentary reading rises at least 1 LU per 2 s: idea -22, team -19, agent -17, mark -13 dB. 4) Swap the mallet/glock land timbre for a softer FM pluck or a bowed-glass pad swell with a longer reverb, and remove the tock layer under the first word. 5) Aim for a momentary of about -13 LUFS at 7.5 s before the inhale dip.
flaws.evidence: audio_events.txt (arp every 0.1 s; kicks 1.6-7.6 s; land runs per word; peak land levels -16.3/-16.0/-16.2/-16.0). audio_eval_full.txt section 1 (momentary list), section 7 (AST and CLAP windows 0-3 s and 6-9 s). Inferred from labels and ML scores, not heard.

flaws.flaw: The brand arrival is under-scored, and the tail is thin and bright. The wall-to-logo glide is the quietest event in the film (-26 dB). Ten 'letter' and 'glass' ticks at 45 ms spacing (22 Hz, about -23 to -19 dB) are the only accent on the title. After tagline:shimmer (-30 dB, 11.3 s) nothing sounds until the sting at 12.7 s: 1.4 s empty, and 0.6 s after the tagline has finished at 12.1 s. The sting is a D6/A6/F#7 chime, then E6/B6/D7 at 13.6 s, at -20 to -27 dB, with F#7 about 2960 Hz and D7 about 2349 Hz sitting in the ear's most sensitive band. Over 12.5-14.5 s the 2-8 kHz share is 23-28% (the only window over 25%), against a median of 5.3%, while RMS falls to -19 and then -22.5 dB. The Audiobox CE and PC scores are lowest in the 12-15 s window (CE 3.87 and 3.99 against an average of 5.2; PC 2.2-2.4). AST gives 'Ding 0.15-0.20' and 'Jingle, tinkle' for that window. Momentary loudness then falls from -15 at 14.0 s to -22 at 14.5 s, and the file ends in digital silence (-200 dBFS).
flaws.why_it_matters: The name and tagline are the point of the film and the last frame has to hold. The audio decays into a tinkly jingle exactly when the brand is on screen, then cuts out in the last half-second while the picture holds. It also plays worst on phone and laptop speakers, where only the bells survive.
flaws.fix: 1) Add a tonic payoff when the title is complete, at about 11.0-11.1 s: a D2/D3 sine plus soft-saw body, -16 dB, 20 ms attack, about 2.5 s decay, with a bell at about -18 dB on the rule draw. 2) Raise the glide from -26 dB to about -18 dB and give it a filtered-noise sweep that lands at about 10.9 s. 3) Slow the letter ticks to 70-90 ms spacing, or play one tick per two letters, so they do not fuse into a 22 Hz flutter. 4) Drop the sting an octave (D5 A5 F#6) and move the first one to about 11.1 s or onto the sheen pass. 5) Keep a warm D-major pad bed and let it fade over at least 1.5 s from about 13.8 s to 15.0 s, so no 0.5 s step is bigger than 3 LU. Target a momentary of about -15 to -16 LUFS for 11.5-14.0 s and a 2-8 kHz share below 15%.
flaws.evidence: audio_events.txt lines 248-280 (glide, letters, shimmer, stings). audio_eval_full.txt section 3 (windows 12.5-15.0 s, 2-8k% and RMS), section 1 (momentary list, last value -22), section 4 (last sample -200 dBFS), section 7 (Audiobox and AST windows 12-15 s). Overview sheet shows the static lockup from about 12 s. Inferred, not heard.

flaws.flaw: The inhale barely dips, and a loud off-grid event sits inside it. Momentary loudness is -15 at 7.5 s and -16 at 8.0 s, so the pre-hit gap lowers loudness by about 1 LU. The riser (noise -19 dB, saw -26) and the reverse swell (-20 dB, from 7.2 s) do not raise the level. The spectrogram shows a bright 20 kHz noise wall from about 7.2 s. The arp stops at 7.8 s and the last kick is at 7.6 s. Then hit:crunch (a Kenney impact at -12.5 dB) sounds at 8.13 s. That is louder than any non-sub element of the build, 270 ms before the downbeat, and not on the 0.4 s kick grid (an isolated triplet-like position). The picture frames at 8.0 s (overview) and 8.300 s (hit_sequence) show the same wall state, so I cannot see what the crunch accompanies.
flaws.why_it_matters: A premium impact is made by contrast: vacuum, then hit. The 8.4 s event reaches only about +6 LU over the build, and the +6 includes a 'gap' that is not really empty. A loud early crunch can also read as a premature or stray hit and steal the downbeat.
flaws.fix: Automate a duck of -9 to -10 dB on pad, bed, riser and reverse swell from 7.85 s to 8.38 s, so the momentary at 8.3 s is about -22 LUFS and the hit reads +10-12 LU. Cut the final 80-120 ms before 8.400 to near-silence (about -40 dB) with the reverse swell peaking at 8.38 s. Lower the 8.13 s crunch from -12.5 to about -22 dB, or tie it to a visible picture event such as the top-row light line, or remove it.
flaws.evidence: audio_events.txt lines 212-220 (last arp 7.8 s, last kick 7.6 s, crunch 8.13 s, riser/swell). audio_eval_full.txt section 1 momentary list (7.5 s: -15, 8.0 s: -16, 8.5 s: -10); spectrogram.png noise wall from about 7.2 s; overview_7.5-14.5s.png and hit_sequence_8.3-9.2s.png. Inferred, not heard.

flaws.flaw: About ten layers all start on the same frame at 8.400 s, and the weight is probably low-frequency. The layers are thump 0 dB, midburst -4.5, chord -6, sub -8.5, crack -9, bell -10, metal -12, glass -13, impactMetal -14 and crash -19, plus lock:bed at -19. Only the bells are staggered (12 ms apart). The sample peak is -2.23 dBFS, so a limiter or master gain is evidently holding the pile-up down. The click detector flags a single-sample step of 0.46 FS (R) and 0.32 FS (L) at exactly 8.400 s, and the max step across the file is 0.61 FS. The true peak (-2.14 dBTP) is at 8.78 s, not at the transient. That suggests the loudest waveform is a sustained low-frequency sum (thump, sub, chord low partials) rather than the crack. The spectrogram shows the film's hottest 20-60 Hz region from 8.4 s to about 9.0 s. Phone and laptop reproduction of the hit specifically is not measured; only the whole-file figure is. Audiobox PQ also dips to its minimum (6.98-7.00) in the 6-10.5 s windows.
flaws.why_it_matters: A simultaneous stack of ten sounds loses definition. A hard-start step at 8.4 s can tick on small speakers or after AAC. If most of the hit energy is 30-80 Hz, the biggest moment may arrive as a thin crack and a few bells on a phone or laptop. Presentations are usually played on laptops, projectors and conference PAs.
flaws.fix: 1) Fade or zero-cross the crack and thump onsets (2-3 ms fade-in) so there is no 0.46 FS step. 2) Stagger the layers: sub drop at 8.400, crack at 8.400, midburst and metal at +5 ms, chord and bells at +12 to +36 ms (as now), crash and glass at +40 to +80 ms. 3) Lower the thump from 0 to about -3 dB and the sub from -8.5 to about -11 dB, then add saturation or a 120-240 Hz harmonic layer on the thump so it speaks through a 150-300 Hz small-speaker high-pass. 4) Re-render and measure the 8.3-9.3 s window separately through a 300 Hz high-pass, with the target hit loss inside the whole-file -1.5 LU.
flaws.evidence: audio_events.txt lines 227-239 (layer gains). audio_eval_full.txt section 4 (click candidates at 8.400 s, max step 0.607 FS), section 1 (true peak at t=8.78 s, sample peak -2.23 dBFS), section 7 (Audiobox windows 6-9 s and 7.5-10.5 s). spectrogram.png 8.4-9.0 s low band. Peak position and sub weighting are inferred.

flaws.flaw: The stereo image goes nearly decorrelated in the post-hit tail and in the sting tail. L/R correlation is +0.19 and +0.17 at 9.0-10.5 s with a mono-fold loss of -2.3 dB. In the last second it is +0.04/+0.05, S/M -0.4 dB, and mono-fold -2.9 to -3.0 dB (the checklist limit is -3 dB, so it just passes). The 12.5-14.5 s windows are also wide (correlation 0.29-0.42, mono-fold -1.5 to -1.9 dB). Inference: the bells, sparks and reverb are heavily widened.
flaws.why_it_matters: This film opens a presentation, and projectors, conference-room PAs and some phones sum to mono. That would lose about 3 dB of the already thin tail, and it risks comb filtering on the bells at the moment the brand holds.
flaws.fix: Narrow the sting and spark bells so S/M stays at or below -6 dB and L/R correlation stays above +0.5 in 12-15 s. Keep the reverb wide but make the dry bells centred. Re-run the mono-fold check and aim for -1.5 dB or better in every window.
flaws.evidence: audio_eval_full.txt section 3 (windows 9.0-10.5 s, 12.5-15.0 s: corrLR, S/M, mono-fold), section 5 (min correlation +0.04).

flaws.flaw: The hook peak sits at exactly t=0 and the energy then falls away before the first word. hook:body -9 dB and hook:bell -10 dB both start at 0.000 s, with ding -14. The 5 ms RMS at the start is -12 dBFS and the first sample is -44 dBFS (the report's 'edges' WARN). Momentary loudness goes -13, -14, -15, -16, -17, -18 across 0-2.5 s, while the picture builds towards ИДЕЯ (flashes at about 1.0-1.5 s). Land notes only reach -16 to -18 dB, so ИДЕЯ lands quieter than the hook.
flaws.why_it_matters: Players and presentation software often start audio late, and AAC priming adds a delay. An onset at exactly 0 ms can be partly lost on playback, so the 'memorable event in the first two seconds' may be missing. The audio is also front-loaded, while the picture's first peak is at 1.0-1.5 s.
flaws.fix: Put 40-60 ms of air or room tone before the hook and move the body and bell peaks to about 0.04-0.06 s. Shorten the hook decay (about 0.4 s). Add a short pad or noise swell from 0.5 s to 1.5 s into ИДЕЯ and raise the land-run peak so the momentary at 1.5 s is no lower than -15 LUFS.
flaws.evidence: audio_events.txt lines 1-5 (hook at 0.000 s), audio_eval_full.txt section 4 (first sample -44 dBFS, 5 ms RMS -12 dBFS) and section 1 momentary list. Overview_0-7s.png (cube, ИДЕЯ flashes at about 1.0-1.5 s).

unverifiable: Actual timbre and taste. Whether the land notes, arp and bells sound toy-like or elegant cannot be judged from event labels and ML scores. AST and CLAP are trained on music, the CLAP prompts are generic, the Audiobox anchors are from only 8 real tracks, and none of them measures brand fit.

Pitches of pad:0-3, bass, kick and hit:chord are not in the labels, so I cannot check them against the key. The stab and land notes, the arps and the sting are the only pitches I can verify. I also cannot tell whether the two simultaneous bass events at 6.400 s (both -12.5 dB, with a kick at -12.5 dB) are a deliberate chord change or a duplicate trigger (+6 dB if identical).

Whether the hit's sub region is actually the loudest component. The peak position (8.78 s) and the spectrogram point to a large 20-60 Hz weight. The report gives only whole-file phone and laptop drops, not the drop in the 8.3-9.3 s window, so hit translation is unmeasured.

Picture sync at the lockup. still_10.50.png shows the mark mid-glide with no title, while the 10.5 s tile in overview_7.5-14.5s.png shows 'HackA' already visible, and the BRIEF says 10.5-11.5 s. I cannot tell whether the letter ticks at 10.62-11.03 s are in sync. I also cannot tell what picture event (a sheen pass) the stings at 12.7 s and 13.6 s are meant to hit.
What happens on screen at 8.13 s (the crunch) and whether it is a deliberate visual anchor. The nearby frames at 8.0 s and 8.300 s look identical.
Stereo placement per event, per-event spectra, reverb and chorus settings, and any AAC pre-echo before 8.4 s. The spectrogram does not show clear smearing, but I cannot check it at this resolution.
Whether the repeated 'row' for 14.0-15.0 s in section 3 (lines 70-71) and the duplicated 12-15 s ML windows are two separate measurements or a reporting artifact.

verdict: A big step up from v1 in look, and the mark and final lockup are clean and faithful. As communication it is weaker than it looks. A stranger gets "idea, team, agent, logo" but has to read 16 px grey text to learn this is a hackathon in Astana. The name arrives about 2.5 s after the visual peak, in the film's darkest and emptiest stretch. The payoff word АГЕНТ gets the shortest on-screen time of the three words. These are timing and hierarchy fixes, not rebuilds. Done well, they would move this from "polished motion piece" to "agency brand intro".
strengths: Frame 0 works as a poster and a hook. One large glowing glass cube in a dark field has a clear focal point. The original small mark and wordmark are on screen from 0.0 s, so the brand is present from the first frame.
Dark, lit, three-dimensional world with real depth, bloom and glass reflections. It directly answers the v1 complaints of flat, inverted and unlit.

ИДЕЯ (about 1.5-2.4 s) and КОМАНДА (about 3.6-4.8 s) are large, legible and held long enough. The wall of cubes forming the pixel letters is an ownable device. The pool becoming words and then the 16x16 mark gives a coherent 'many parts unite' metaphor.

The mark is built from the same cubes as the words and carries the carved figure (8.3 s still), so the story arrives at the real brand symbol rather than a generic one. The glide-left and flatten into the flat vector mark (10.5 to 11.0 to 12.5 s stills) is a good bridge from 3D to a usable logo.

Final lockup (about 11.6-15 s, about 3.4 s hold) is clean: the original blue mark, white Manrope 'HackAlem' with a cyan 'AI', a rule, and the mono tagline. The name is spelled as required. There are no dates, sums or head-counts.
Russian words are correctly spelled and capitalised (ИДЕЯ, КОМАНДА, АГЕНТ, ХАКАТОН, АСТАНА). Nothing in the copy contains an error.

The event list shows letter landings, the 8.4 s hit and the title letters all cued to the picture, and the hit_sequence frames show the flash and ripple landing exactly at 8.40 s. The audio checklist is 14/16 OK, with no clipping and about -14.7 LUFS.

flaws.timecode: whole film (corner tagline 0-9.7 s; lockup tagline 11.5-15 s)
flaws.flaw: What the thing is, and where, is carried only by a tiny low-contrast mono tagline, and the story words do not say it. The tagline 'AGENTIC-AI ХАКАТОН · АСТАНА' sits in the top-right corner at about 11 px cap height at 1280 (about 16 px at 1080p, about 1.5% of frame height). It is pale grey-blue on navy, and cubes fly across it (1.2 s still). In the lockup it is still the smallest text, roughly 1:4 against the title's cap height. The three hero words are bare nouns with no connector or verb. 'АГЕНТ' alone in Russian reads as spy or insurance agent, not AI agent. The brief's 'people uniting to turn ideas into AI agents' never appears in words.
flaws.why_it_matters: A stranger sees ИДЕЯ, КОМАНДА, АГЕНТ and a logo. They can only learn 'hackathon', 'Astana' and 'agentic AI' from text they cannot read on a phone (phone_size_360px.png) or a conference projector. The corner tagline also pre-spoils the ending's tagline reveal, so that reveal carries no news.
flaws.fix: 1) Make the third word 'ИИ-АГЕНТ' (or 'AI-АГЕНТ'), or add a small 'ИИ' before it, so the word cannot be read as a spy. 2) Show causality between the words with an arrow or '+' / '→' glyph built from cubes streaking between words in the 2.4-3.0 s and 4.8-5.8 s transitions. 3) Delete the corner tagline, or keep it only as the corner logo. Instead, at about 11.1-12.1 s set the tagline at 40-44 px at 1920x1080 (cap height about 30 px), colour #E6F4FF at 90% or more, tracking 0.12-0.14 em. Put 'ХАКАТОН · АСТАНА' on its own line if it needs more size. 4) Optionally give 'АСТАНА' its own beat at the hit, for example brief large type on the ripple.
flaws.evidence: still_00.00.png (zoomed corner crop; tagline cap height about 11 px at 1280), still_01.20.png (cube crossing the tagline), still_12.50.png (tagline about 22 px cap height vs title about 90 px), phone_size_360px.png (tagline illegible in every tile), BRIEF.md ('turn ideas into AI agents').

flaws.flaw: The visual peak carries only the wordless mark. The name arrives about 2.5 s later, in the film's emptiest stretch. The flash at 8.4-8.6 s has mean frame luminance of about 114. The wall then tilts and glides, and the corner logo and tagline disappear at about 9.7 s. At 10.50 s there is no text on screen at all, only a small mark in a half-empty frame, at mean luminance of about 32, the lowest of the second half. 'HackAlem' starts rising at about 10.6 s and 'AI' is still blurred at 11.00 s. The name is fully readable only at about 11.6 s.
flaws.why_it_matters: The strongest moment of the film, with the biggest sound hit, imprints a square. The thing the customer asked for ('brand on screen too briefly', name recognisable) is spent after the energy has dropped. A presenter who cuts the film off at about 10 s has shown no name at all except the 17%-wide corner wordmark.
flaws.fix: Tie the name to the hit. Option A: let the title letters assemble on the 8.5-9.3 s ripple, with 'HackAlem' flashing in letter by letter on the shockwave and the mark gliding left under it. Option B: keep the order but pull it forward. Start the glide at 9.2 s, start the title at 9.5 s, and have the full lockup by about 10.6 s. In either case do not remove the corner logo and tagline at 9.7 s. Cross-fade them into the lockup so no frame is text-free. The lockup would then hold about 4.4 s instead of 3.4 s.
flaws.evidence: still_10.50.png (no text, mark alone), still_11.00.png ('AI' blurred), still_08.50.png vs still_10.50.png (mean luminance about 114 vs 32), overview_7.5-14.5s.png (10.0 s and 10.5 s cells), audio_events.txt (letters at 10.62-11.03 s, spark tail fading from -18 to -27 dB).

flaws.flaw: The payoff word of the story has the shortest fully formed time. ИДЕЯ holds about 0.9 s and КОМАНДА about 1.2 s. АГЕНТ is fully legible for about 0.6 s. At 5.0 s the cubes are a scatter, at 5.5 s the word is half built, and at 6.5 s it is already swirling. The word with the most abstract meaning has the least time to be decoded in a pixel face.
flaws.why_it_matters: The climax of 'Идея → Команда → Агент' is the last step, and it is also where a viewer most needs a beat to decode a pixel-font word. Reading three words in about 7 s should feel like a rhythm of rising weight, not a rushed third beat. If the word is missed, the mark swirl at 6.4-7.8 s has nothing to resolve.
flaws.fix: Re-time so each word is fully formed for at least 0.9 s, with АГЕНТ longest. For example, shorten the КОМАНДА hold from 1.2 s to 0.9 s and start the АГЕНТ assembly at about 4.5 s so it is complete by 5.5 s. Hold it until about 6.5 s (about 1.0 s). Start the swirl into the mark at 6.6 s and shave the 7.8-8.4 s 'inhale' or the swirl by about 0.2 s to compensate. Avoid cubes drifting in front of the word during the hold, as in the 6.0 s cell.
flaws.evidence: overview_0-7s.png (cells at 4.5, 5.0, 5.5, 6.0, 6.5 s: fully legible only at about 6.0 s), BRIEF.md timing (assembly 4.8-5.8 s, swirl from about 6.4 s), audio_events.txt (land:agent events at 5.3-5.8 s, then riser from 6.4 s).

flaws.timecode: 0-3 s and whole film (background and cube colour)
flaws.flaw: The film is not on the brand's actual dark base, and the first 3 s are off-palette. The end-frame background samples at about (0,23,58) to (0,33,71) with a frame mean of about (7,41,81), a saturated navy that is clearly brighter and bluer than brand #060B16 (6,11,22). The cubes in the first 3 s are milky teal at frame 0 (about 110,200,225) and ice-white in ИДЕЯ (about 200,225,245), not #009AF0 or #00C8FF. Brand blue only appears from КОМАНДА and in the mark. The site's signature, a blue volumetric beam from above on a near-black scene, is barely present in the film. The corner wordmark is lowercase 'hackalem.ai', while the title is 'HackAlem AI'. Both are spelled correctly for their role, but the viewer sees two forms of the name for 15 s.
flaws.why_it_matters: The customer's v1 complaint was 'inverted vs the dark brand'. This fixes the inversion but not the brand's own colour. The film ends on a lockup that will be cut to or from a presentation built on #060B16. A visible base-colour mismatch at that cut looks like two different brands. The name is the one thing the brief says must stay fixed, so showing two spellings invites a question from the client.
flaws.fix: Grade the whole film to a #060B16 base. Keep the beam and glow as additive #009AF0 and #00C8FF, with the vignette to near-black. Make the ИДЕЯ cubes #00C8FF emissive with white only on edge highlights, and reserve pure white for the hit. Keep the end lockup background identical to the presentation template. If the corner wordmark is the client's official horizontal logo, say so in the handoff note. Otherwise swap it for the mark alone in the corner.
flaws.evidence: Pixel sampling of still_00.00.png, still_02.20.png, still_12.50.png and still_14.50.png; BRIEF.md brand facts (#060B16, #009AF0, #00C8FF, volumetric beam); still_00.00.png logo crop ('hackalem.ai') vs still_12.50.png ('HackAlem AI').

flaws.flaw: The hold frame is not fully resolved as a lockup, and it is the frame the presentation will sit on. The tagline (x 432-1107) is shorter than the title (to about x 1167 at 1280), and the rule ends at about x 803, so three right edges do not line up. The text block is top-aligned to the mark: the mark centre is at y 360, but the title, rule and tagline block (y 230-422) centres at about y 326. That is about 34 px at 1280 (about 51 px at 1080p), so the block floats high. The bottom 70 px of the mark has no neighbour. The mark is about 3x the title cap height. The soft sheen across the mark that the brief promises is not visible between the 12.5 s and 14.5 s stills.
flaws.why_it_matters: This frame will be shown for far longer than 15 s, and it is the one an agency's work is judged on. Ragged edges and an off-centre text block are exactly the kind of craft slips a brand team notices on a static hold. A hold with no visible life may also read as frozen when used as a title slide.
flaws.fix: Measure and align to a grid. Set the tagline tracking so its right edge matches the title's right edge (or shorten the title and tagline to a common width). Make the rule the same width as the title. Vertically centre the three-line block on the mark, or reduce the mark to about 2x cap height. Add a perceptible but slow sheen (10-15% brightness band, about 2.5 s travel) and keep slow star drift so the hold stays alive.
flaws.evidence: still_12.50.png and still_14.50.png (measured bounding boxes: mark 100-369 x 225-494, title to about 1167, rule 431-803, tagline 432-1107 x 399-422); overview_7.5-14.5s.png (12.5-14.5 s cells look identical).

flaws.flaw: After the flash, the light coming through the carved figure decays into desaturated steel grey. Interior cells sample at about (100,143,173), (111,153,186) and (72,118,155) in still_09.20.png, instead of brand blue or dark. In the 9.0 and 9.5 s overview cells the figure region reads as a dull grey panel. The wall is also tilted at this point, so the mark looks like a dim screen for about 0.6 s.
flaws.why_it_matters: Grey is not in the palette, and the carved figure is the most distinctive part of the mark. It looks muddy for the first beauty-shot moment right after the peak, where a client will look hardest.
flaws.fix: Keep the backlight saturated. Tint the light through the figure #00C8FF falling to #009AF0, and avoid bloom or tone-mapping that desaturates it. Or let the backlight fall to the dark base within about 0.3 s so the figure reads as a dark carved shape, as in the flat mark. Check the 8.7-9.6 s frames at full size for grey cells.
flaws.evidence: still_09.20.png (pixel samples), overview_7.5-14.5s.png (9.0 s and 9.5 s cells), hit_sequence_8.3-9.2s.png (last row).

unverifiable: Motion quality and smoothness, including whether the 0.3-1.5 s fly-in and the 8.4 s hit feel energetic and not choppy. Only stills and contact sheets exist, and v1's chief complaint was choppy motion.

Whether the sound feels premium or reads as a retro-game jingle. The measurements are mixed: AST scores 'Video game music' at 0.48 in the 6-9 s window, and CLAP ranks '8-bit chiptune' at 0.39 against 'clean premium tech logo sting' at 0.45 overall. Those are classifier scores, not listening. Loudness and spectrum (-14.7 LUFS, no clipping) say nothing about whether the hit feels like a hit. The brief also warns that nobody has listened.

Whether the corner wordmark 'hackalem.ai' (lowercase, pixel 'k') and the typeset 'HackAlem AI' with cyan 'AI' match the client's official logo files and lockup rules. I cannot compare to hackalem.ai from the material.
Whether the faint cell grid visible inside the flat vector mark in the end lockup is in the client's original vector. It may be a render artefact.
Whether the 'soft sheen' in the 12.1-15 s hold exists and how visible it is. The 12.5 s and 14.5 s stills look identical, and a still cannot show a travelling highlight.

Whether the string for 'АГЕНТ' in the source uses a Cyrillic А or a Latin A. BRIEF.md spells it 'AГЕНТ' (Latin-looking A), and the two letters are visually identical in the pixel font. It matters for subtitles, search and accessibility, not for the picture.
Whether text overlap (cubes crossing the corner tagline and wordmark) is frequent or occasional. The stills show it at 1.2 s and about 6.8 s, but I cannot sample every frame.

verdict: A clear step up from v1: it is dark, lit and atmospheric, and the cube-built Russian words and the final lockup read well even at 360 px. It is not yet a premium-agency opener for a phone feed. The brand name is not legible until about 10.6 s. The peak is a short bleach-out on a wall that fills only about a third of the frame width. The payoff word АГЕНТ gets the shortest hold of the three. The first 0.8 s and the last 3 s have almost no motion, and until the mark appears the look is the stock "glowing cubes in a blue void" treatment. A skeptical thumb leaves at about 2-4 s, having seen a pretty cube cloud and two words with no readable brand and no real event. That viewer never reaches the hit at 8.4 s. Judged as a presentation opener on a big screen it is solid, around 7.
strengths: Frame 0 has one clear focal point: a single lit cube in a field of dark glass debris. It reads instantly at 360 px (phone panel 1) and fixes v1's inverted, flat look. The film is genuinely dark (92% of pixels below luma 40 at frame 0) with depth of field, motion blur and rim light.

ИДЕЯ (about 1.5-2.4 s) is the strongest legible image: ice-white glowing cube-letters that read cleanly at 360 px and are the most memorable still in the film. КОМАНДА (3.5-4.8 s) also reads at phone size, though dimmer.

The film works as one continuous object. The sheets and stills show no hard cuts; the same cubes go from scatter to word to word to wall to flat mark. The wall at 8.0-8.3 (lit cube wall with a dark carved figure) is a distinctive, ownable image.

The hit is a real event, not just a claim. Mean luma goes from about 44 (8.367) to 87 (8.400) to 114 (8.433), and 12% of pixels exceed luma 200 at 8.50. The audio event list puts the hit at the same 8.400 s, so picture and sound are aligned.

The final lockup has good hierarchy. Title cap height is about 25 px at 360 px wide, 'AI' is in brand cyan, and the flat mark matches the 3D wall figure, so the wall-to-logo continuity is believable. It is clean and can hold under a presentation.
The Cyrillic pixel glyphs are well drawn, and the colour escalation white to blue to cyan to mark to flat brand blue gives a sense of development even with sound off.

flaws.timecode: 0.0-3.0 s and corner overlay 0-9.7 s (brand name first full-size at about 10.6-11.0 s)
flaws.flaw: A feed viewer cannot tell what this is or who it is from until 70% of the way through. The only brand cue for the first 10 s is the corner wordmark, about 7 px cap height at 360 px. The corner tagline 'AGENTIC-AI ХАКАТОН · АСТАНА' is about 3 px cap height at 360 px, so it is a dotted line (about 11 px cap at 1280 wide). It then repeats verbatim in the end lockup. The film also shows the name as lowercase 'hackalem.ai' for 9.7 s and 'HackAlem AI' only at the end. The full title lands at 10.62-11.03 s, so anyone who swipes at 2-4 s saw cubes and two Russian words with no readable brand. Frame 0 itself is quiet (one hero cube, nothing moving into frame) and the 0.5 s frame is the emptiest in the film (95.5% of pixels below luma 40, cube shrunk to a small dot).
flaws.why_it_matters: The brief wants the name recognisable and a memorable event in the first 2 s. On a phone the first 3 s carry no brand and no readable context, and a 16:9 clip shrinks to a 360x203 strip, so small type is lost entirely. The film's best hook, the ИДЕЯ word, shows a concept with no owner.
flaws.fix: 1) Scale the corner wordmark about 1.6x (to about 12 px cap at 360 px) and delete the corner tagline, since it duplicates the end lockup and is illegible. 2) Add a 0.6-0.8 s full-size 'HackAlem AI' name flash during the КОМАНДА hold (about 3.7-4.5 s) or tie the name to the first word, at roughly 90 px cap height. 3) Make frame 0 carry motion: have the hero cube already moving or pulsing, and show the first fly-ins starting by 0.15 s instead of the sparse 0.3-0.8 s lull. 4) Use one brand spelling, 'HackAlem AI', in the corner.
flaws.evidence: phone_size_360px.png panels 1-5 (corner tagline an unreadable smudge); still_00.00 and still_00.50 (pixel stats: 92.3% and 95.5% of pixels below luma 40); still_10.50 (no title) and still_11.00 (title mid-reveal); audio_events.txt letter:0-9 at 10.62-11.03 s; overview_0-7s tiles 0.0-0.5 s

flaws.flaw: The peak is a short whiteout, not a striking climax. Mean luma doubles in one frame (about 44 to 87 between 8.367 and 8.400) and peaks at about 114-120 from 8.43 to 8.5. The wall goes pale, milky white-lavender: the brand blue is lost except the four corner cells, and the cube gloss and carved-figure edges disappear into haze (still_08.50). It sits above luma 100 for only about 0.3 s, then falls to 88 by 8.83 and 65 by 9.2. The wall is only about 34% of frame width before the hit and about 43% at the peak (275 of 640 px in the hit sequence tiles), so at 360 px it is roughly a 120-150 px glowing square. The 'ripple through the wall' is not distinguishable in the frames: you see a scale pop, a whiteout and slightly curved edges at 8.533. After the flash the wall shrinks, tilts and dims (9.0-9.2) instead of delivering a beauty shot.
flaws.why_it_matters: This is the one moment the whole film builds toward, and on a small screen it reads as a brief flash on a small pale square. The brand colour disappears at exactly the moment the brand mark is revealed, and the carved figure (the key brand asset) is least legible at the peak. It also arrives at 8.4 s, after most feed viewers have left.
flaws.fix: Keep the flash from bleaching the wall. Clamp wall emissive and bloom so cubes stay between #009AF0 and #00C8FF, and let white appear only in the carved-figure holes and the cell seams. Cap full-screen haze so mean luma peaks at about 90, not 120. Add a visible distance-based ripple, with a per-cell delay of about 25-30 ms radiating from the figure, so a wave of brightness and cube depth sweeps outward over 0.4 s. Scale the wall about 1.5x on the hit (to roughly 65-70% of frame width) and hold the bright blue state for about 0.5 s instead of 0.3 s. Also make the pre-hit wall bigger (about 45-50% of frame width at 8.0-8.3) so it reads on a phone.

flaws.timecode: 5.8-6.4 s (АГЕНТ), glare at about 1.2 s, cloud at 6.4-7.4 s
flaws.flaw: The payoff word of the Идея, Команда, Агент chain is held fully formed for only about 0.5 s. By the audio event list the last letter lands at 5.8 s, the stab is at 5.9 s and the riser/swirl starts at 6.4 s. ИДЕЯ holds about 0.9 s and КОМАНДА about 1.1 s. At 6.5 the word is already shredding, and at 5.5 (still_05.50) it is half-formed. Arriving cubes also flare white-hot and block letters while they land: at 1.2 s the Е and Я of ИДЕЯ are hidden by glare, and 5.5 s is blown out the same way. At 360 px the 6.4-7.4 s swirl (phone panel 4) is an unreadable cube cloud.
flaws.why_it_matters: The film's story is carried by the three words, especially with sound off, and the third word is the one that should land hardest. A phone viewer has about 0.5 s to read five Cyrillic letters while they are still glowing. The rhythm also feels hurried exactly where the film should be building toward the mark.
flaws.fix: Move the swirl start from 6.4 to about 6.9 s so АГЕНТ holds at least 1.0-1.1 s fully assembled, like КОМАНДА. Pay for it by shortening the swirl-to-mark leg (6.4-7.8 s, 1.4 s) to about 0.9 s. Cut the landing glare: reduce emissive/bloom on cubes that are still moving by about 40% so glyphs stay readable, and let the flash happen on the stab after the last cube lands.

flaws.flaw: Five soft spots. (a) 0.0-0.8: one cube and sparse debris, with the 0.5 s frame nearly empty. (b) 8.300 to 8.367 is a frozen pair of frames (mean abs diff 1.33/255), the 'inhale', then a one-frame 44/255 jump to the flash, which reads as a stutter on a phone. (c) 9.2-10.6: the wall shrinks and dims, the corner labels drop out at about 9.7, and the wall glides left to a lone flat mark. At 10.5 it sits at 21-48% of frame width with the right two thirds empty and no title yet. (d) The title is announced as 'letter by letter' but all 10 letters land in about 0.4 s (10.62-11.03 s, 45 ms apart), so it reads as a pop. (e) 12.1-15.0 is effectively a still: 12.50 vs 14.50 differ by 0.59/255 mean abs (0.29 in the mark region), so the promised sheen is imperceptible at least at those two instants.
flaws.why_it_matters: Together these make a loud, busy 1.4 s peak surrounded by lulls; for a feed viewer they are the places to swipe. The 3 s static hold is right for a slide master but is 3 s of nothing in a feed.
flaws.fix: (a) Start with the hero cube already drifting and 3-5 cubes streaking into frame from 0.1 s. (b) Keep the wall alive through the inhale: 2-3 degrees of slow rotation and a small cell shimmer so frames are never identical, and ramp luma 1.5x over 3-4 frames before the hit instead of a hard jump. (c) Start the title entrance at about 9.7 s, overlapping the glide, so the screen is never a lone mark on the left. (d) Stretch the letter stagger from 45 ms to about 90 ms (about 0.9 s total). (e) Add a slow 3-4% push-in or a stronger sheen sweep across the mark between 12.5 and 14.5 s so the hold breathes.
flaws.evidence: hit_sequence tile diffs (1.33 for 8.300 to 8.367; 44.66 for 8.367 to 8.400); still_00.50; still_10.50; overview_7.5-14.5s tiles 10.0-12.5; audio_events.txt letter:0-9 at 45 ms intervals; pixel diff of still_12.50 vs still_14.50 (mean abs 0.59/255)

flaws.flaw: Until the mark appears the look is generic. Glossy cubes with bloom, bokeh dust and a monochrome blue gradient void are familiar stock 3D motion-graphics territory. The same beat repeats three times at a near-metronomic 2.4 s cadence (scatter, assemble word, hold, scatter), so by the third word the trick is predictable. Nothing says Astana, people, or agents. 'Agentic AI' appears only as tiny mono type that cannot be read on a phone. The single hero cube from frame 0 is never used again: it vanishes into the pool, and the memorable image is not the brand mark.
flaws.why_it_matters: A premium agency intro needs one ownable idea that a viewer could recall and describe. Here the recall is 'glowing cubes spell words', which belongs to many templates. The brand's carved figure only appears at 8.0-8.3 s, past most feed viewers' patience.
flaws.fix: Make the frame-0 hero cube a character. Give it a different material from the pool (cyan #00C8FF emissive core), follow it through the three words as the cube that 'starts' each assembly, and have it land in the carved figure's head cell at 8.4 s so it triggers the hit, then keep that one cell softly pulsing in the end lockup. Break the three-word metronome by varying the assembly style: ИДЕЯ from a single point, КОМАНДА from sides, АГЕНТ from depth. Also show the carved figure early, for example as a 0.3 s negative-space flash in the КОМАНДА to АГЕНТ transition, so the brand's visual signature is seen before 8 s.
flaws.evidence: overview_0-7s.png (three assembly cycles at 0.3-1.5, 2.4-3.6 and 4.8-5.8 s); still_00.00 (hero cube) vs overview tiles from 1.0 s on (hero cube absorbed into the pool); still_08.30 (first clear figure); BRIEF.md concept description

unverifiable: Real-time motion quality (smoothness, judder, ease curves). I only had stills, 0.5 s sheets and one 33 ms-step hit sequence, so how the cube fly-ins and swirl feel in motion is not judged.

Sound as heard. I cannot judge timbre, whether it is thin or toy-like, or whether it helps the sense of development. Measurements only say integrated -14.66 LUFS, no clipping, 23.9% of energy below 150 Hz, and only -1.5 LU lost through a phone-speaker high-pass. The audio events line up with the picture (hit at 8.400 s). Sound-off viewing is judged from the picture only.

Timecode disagreement between sources. overview_7.5-14.5s tile '10.5s' already shows 'HackA' blurred with the mark at its final position and tile '11.0s' shows the complete 'HackAlem AI'. still_10.50 shows no title and still_11.00 shows 'AI' still fading in. audio_events.txt (letters 10.62-11.03 s) agrees with the stills. The 8.5 and 9.2 frames match across sources. I judged title timing from the stills and audio, but I cannot tell if the sheet is offset by about 0.4 s after 10 s.
Whether the ripple through the wall at 8.4 s exists as a coherent wave. Between the 33 ms steps I see only a scale pop, haze and slight edge curvature at 8.533; a fast wave could fall between frames.
Whether the 'soft sheen' during the 12-15 s hold is visible anywhere. I measured only 12.50 vs 14.50 (mean abs 0.59/255); the sheen may occur at another instant.
How a 16:9 clip is shown in the actual feed (letterboxed, cropped or zoomed), and which platform UI covers the top corners. The 360 px sheet assumes the full frame at width 360.

Whether the first-frame cube reads as 'glass' to a viewer. In the still it looks like frosted matte turquoise plastic with soft edge highlights, with no visible refraction; this is subjective and I could not judge it moving.
